title: Left properness of the Bergner model structure
statement: Use small simplicial categories and the Bergner model structure of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], whose weak equivalences are Dwyer--Kan equivalences. This model structure is left proper: for any Dwyer--Kan equivalence $u:A\to B$ and cofibration $i:A\to D$, the canonical functor $D\to B\amalg_A D$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. The pushout is in the category of small simplicial categories with arbitrary object functions on enriched functors. No local Kan hypothesis is imposed on $A,B,D$.

source.place: Proposition A.3.2.4, printed pp. 858–860, specialized to simplicial sets with the Kan–Quillen model structure; its conclusion includes left properness. No Stacks tag states this result. Read online and in an existing text extraction; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Let $I$ be the boundary-arrow and new-object generators in [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. An $I$-injective functor is exactly a functor surjective on objects and a trivial Kan fibration on each mapping set: lifting against the new-object generator gives surjectivity, and lifting against $U(\partial\Delta^n)\to U(\Delta^n)$ is precisely boundary lifting on a specified mapping set. These are exactly the Bergner trivial fibrations of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. In one direction, local trivial fibrations are local weak equivalences and induce bijections on mapping components. Surjectivity on objects then gives essential surjectivity and lifts an isomorphism in $\pi_0$ by choosing an object over its target and its unique preimage class; full faithfulness makes that class invertible. Conversely, a Bergner trivial fibration is locally a trivial Kan fibration, and essential surjectivity followed by equivalence lifting makes its object function surjective. Thus Bergner cofibrations equal $I$-cofibrations. The cited small-object factorization writes the given $i:A\to D$ as $A\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{p}D$ with $j$ an $I$-cell map and $p$ $I$-injective. Lifting $i$ against $p$ gives a section $s:D\to E$ under $A$ with $ps=1_D$, so $i$ is a retract of $j$ under $A$.

source.place: p.858, generators preceding A.3.2.4; generator lifting and the elementary retract argument

proof.text: It suffices first to treat $j$. Well-order the cells in every coproduct attachment and adjoin them successively. The resulting colimit equals the simultaneous attachment: functors out of either are exactly a functor out of the old category and a compatible extension for each cell. This also holds for every subsequent attachment by the same universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. We can therefore use a small ordinal sequence $C_0=A$, $C_\theta=E$, continuous at limits, with one generator pushed out at each successor. Set $B_\alpha=B\amalg_A C_\alpha$ and let $u_\alpha:C_\alpha\to B_\alpha$ be the canonical functor, so $u_0=u$. The same colimit universal property identifies $B_{\alpha+1}$ with the pushout attaching that same generator to $B_\alpha$, and makes the $B$ sequence continuous. We prove by transfinite induction that $u_\alpha$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. Each successor transition in either sequence is injective on objects and on every old mapping set: for a new object this is its isolated-object description; for an arrow cell this follows from [lem-coef-scat-arrow-cell-word-filtration].

source.place: pp.858-860, reduction to generating attachments, extended to relative cell maps by their colimit universal properties

proof.text: For the generator $\varnothing\to\{0\}$, the successor categories are $C_\alpha\amalg\{*\}$ and $B_\alpha\amalg\{*\}$, with $*$ a fresh isolated object. The new endomorphism set is $\Delta^0$ and all mixed mapping sets are empty. The new comparison is $u_\alpha$ on old mapping sets and the identity on the other ones. It is locally a weak equivalence. Essential surjectivity on old objects is the inductive hypothesis; the new object is its own image. Hence $u_{\alpha+1}$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence, using exactly the criterion in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison].

source.place: p.859, first case: adjoining a new isolated object

proof.text: Now attach $U(K)\to U(L)$, with $K=\partial\Delta^n$, $L=\Delta^n$. Fix $w,z$ in $C_\alpha$. Apply [lem-coef-scat-arrow-cell-word-filtration] to $C_\alpha$ and $B_\alpha$, with the target coordinates the images of $w,z,x,y$. It gives natural filtrations $P_k,P'_k$ and pushout squares $N_k\to M_k$, $N'_k\to M'_k$. In its notation the maps of upper rows are $H_k\times Q_k\to H'_k\times Q_k$ and $H_k\times L^k\to H'_k\times L^k$. Both are weak homotopy equivalences. Indeed each mapping-set factor of $H_k\to H'_k$ is one by induction. Realization preserves finite products by [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits]. For a finite product, paths, based maps of spheres and their based homotopies are tuples of those in the factors; thus components and homotopy groups are products. This proves directly, from the weak-equivalence definition in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], that a finite product of weak equivalences, including multiplication by any fixed simplicial set, is a weak equivalence. Empty factors present no exception. Thus it applies with the same $Q_k$ or $L^k$ in source and target; no assertion about preservation of unions by weak equivalences is being assumed.

source.place: pp.859-860, mapping-word products and the two maps N_C to N_D and M_C to M_D

proof.text: Induct on $k$. At $k=0$, $P_0=C_\alpha(w,z)\to B_\alpha(u_\alpha w,u_\alpha z)=P'_0$ is a weak equivalence. For $k\geq1$, the two spans $P_{k-1}\leftarrow N_k\hookrightarrow M_k$ and $P'_{k-1}\leftarrow N'_k\hookrightarrow M'_k$ have all objects cofibrant in the Kan model structure: every simplicial set is cofibrant since its initial map is degreewise injective [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Their designated right legs are monomorphisms and hence cofibrations. Their three comparison maps are weak equivalences by the induction on $k$ and step 4. Clause (b) of [lem-coef-model-cofibrant-colimit-comparison] therefore gives $P_k\to P'_k$ a weak equivalence. Crucially the other legs need not be cofibrations, and no mapping space is assumed Kan.

source.place: p.860, induction on the word filtration; cube-lemma formulation of the source homotopy-pushout comparison

proof.text: The word filtrations are continuous $\omega$-sequences of monomorphisms, starting at cofibrant simplicial sets, by [lem-coef-scat-arrow-cell-word-filtration] and the Kan cofibration characterization [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Clause (c) of [lem-coef-model-cofibrant-colimit-comparison], with $\theta=\omega$, gives a weak equivalence on their colimits. These are precisely the successor mapping sets, so $u_{\alpha+1}$ is locally a weak equivalence. Arrow attachments change no objects. For any object of $B_{\alpha+1}$, the essential-surjectivity witness in $\pi_0B_\alpha$ maps to a witness in $\pi_0B_{\alpha+1}$, since a functor preserves an inverse and its two equations. Thus $u_{\alpha+1}$ is essentially surjective and is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence by [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison].

source.place: p.860, passage from finite word stages to all words and essential surjectivity

proof.text: For completeness, the limit categories in these cell sequences are computed by unions of object sets and degreewise unions of mapping sets once their two objects have appeared. To verify this, represent each object or simplex at a stage; any finite list of representatives occurs at a common larger stage. Define a composition there. Its value is independent of that stage since all transition functors preserve composition. Associativity, units and commutation with simplicial operators hold there and hence in the union. Compatible functors from the stages give a unique functor from this union, on the represented objects and simplices. This is exactly the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Injectivity at successors was proved in step 2; the union construction preserves it at limits. Consequently every transition in either sequence is injective on objects and locally a monomorphism, and mapping-set diagrams on a tail containing a chosen pair are continuous at limit ordinals.

source.place: Remark A.3.2.3 and A.3.2.4; explicit finite-operation construction of the ordinal colimits used here

proof.text: Let $\lambda\leq\theta$ be a nonzero limit ordinal and assume the comparison is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence at every earlier stage. Any pair of objects of $C_\lambda$ appears in some $C_\beta$, $\beta<\lambda$. On the tail $\beta\leq\alpha<\lambda$ their mapping sets and the mapping sets of their images form two continuous sequences of cofibrations between cofibrant simplicial sets by step 7 and [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Their component maps are weak equivalences by induction. This tail has small nonzero limit order type; clause (c) of [lem-coef-model-cofibrant-colimit-comparison] applies and gives a weak equivalence between the union mapping sets, which are the required mapping sets at $\lambda$. Every object of $B_\lambda$ appears at some earlier stage and has there an isomorphism in $\pi_0$ to an image object. The functor to the union carries that isomorphism and its inverse to the same witness at $\lambda$. Hence $u_\lambda$ is essentially surjective, and the Dwyer--Kan criterion of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] finishes the limit step. Along with steps 3-6 and the given $u_0$, transfinite induction proves $u_\theta:E\to B\amalg_A E$ a weak equivalence.

source.place: Remark A.3.2.3 and A.3.2.4, closure along the continuous relative-cell sequence

proof.text: Finally use $s:D\to E$ and $p:E\to D$ under $A$ from step 1. The pushout universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] induces maps $B\amalg_A D\to B\amalg_A E\to B\amalg_A D$ whose composite is the identity, since this is true after each coprojection. Together with $s,p$ these exhibit $D\to B\amalg_A D$ as a retract in the arrow category of $E\to B\amalg_A E$. Weak equivalences are retract closed in the model-category convention of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], so the former is a weak equivalence too. In the Bergner structure this says exactly that the canonical map in the item is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. The proof made no fibrancy assumption on $A,B,D$ and allowed arbitrary object functions throughout.

source.place: p.858, weakly saturated cofibration class; retract completion of the generating-cell argument
